title: Benefits Enrollment Rates by Department
prompt: Your HR platform tracks employees and their benefits enrollment records. Each employee belongs to a department, and each enrollment record has a status ('pending', 'completed', 'declined'). You need to generate a report showing every department that has at least one employee hired in 2024 or later, along with the count of completed enrollments submitted by those employees during Q1 2024 (January 1 through March 31, 2024). Departments with qualifying employees but zero completed Q1 2024 enrollments must still appear with a count of 0. Return columns: department_name, employee_count (the number of employees in that department hired in 2024 or later), completed_q1_enrollments (the count of completed enrollment records submitted in Q1 2024 by those employees). Order by department_name ascending.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE departments (department_id INT PRIMARY KEY, department_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE employees (employee_id INT PRIMARY KEY, department_id INT NOT NULL, employee_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, hire_date DATE NOT NULL, FOREIGN KEY (department_id) REFERENCES departments(department_id)); CREATE TABLE benefit_enrollments (enrollment_id INT PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INT NOT NULL, enrollment_status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, submitted_date DATE NOT NULL, FOREIGN KEY (employee_id) REFERENCES employees(employee_id));
example_input_data: INSERT INTO departments (department_id, department_name) VALUES (1, 'Engineering'), (2, 'Sales'), (3, 'Marketing'); INSERT INTO employees (employee_id, department_id, employee_name, hire_date) VALUES (101, 1, 'Alice', '2024-01-15'), (102, 1, 'Bob', '2024-02-20'), (103, 2, 'Carol', '2024-03-10'), (104, 2, 'Dave', '2023-11-05'), (105, 3, 'Eve', '2024-04-01'); INSERT INTO benefit_enrollments (enrollment_id, employee_id, enrollment_status, submitted_date) VALUES (1, 101, 'completed', '2024-01-20'), (2, 101, 'completed', '2024-02-15'), (3, 102, 'completed', '2024-03-25'), (4, 102, 'pending', '2024-02-10'), (5, 103, 'declined', '2024-03-15'), (6, 104, 'completed', '2024-01-12'), (7, 105, 'completed', '2024-05-01');

composite_moves: LEFT-side filter on employees.hire_date >= '2024-01-01' placed in WHERE (removes employees hired before 2024)
LEFT JOIN employees to benefit_enrollments keeping all qualifying employees
RIGHT-side filter on benefit_enrollments: enrollment_status = 'completed' AND submitted_date >= '2024-01-01' AND < '2024-04-01' placed in ON (preserves employees with no matching enrollments)
COUNT(benefit_enrollments.enrollment_id) per department to count qualifying enrollments (0 when none)
GROUP BY department, aggregate employee_count and enrollment count
HAVING employee_count > 0 to keep only departments with at least one 2024-hired employee

hints: You need to find which employees were hired in 2024 or later, then count their completed Q1 2024 enrollments per department while keeping departments that have no such enrollments.

The filter on hire_date restricts which employees you consider (it's about the LEFT side); the filters on enrollment_status and submitted_date restrict which enrollments you count (they're about the RIGHT side). Think about where each filter should go so departments with qualifying employees but zero matching enrollments still appear.

Use a LEFT JOIN from employees to benefit_enrollments, place `enrollment_status = 'completed' AND submitted_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND submitted_date < DATE '2024-04-01'` in the ON clause, place `hire_date >= DATE '2024-01-01'` in the WHERE clause, then GROUP BY department and COUNT the enrollment_id column (which is NULL when no match). Use HAVING to keep only departments with at least one 2024-hired employee.
answer_key: SELECT d.department_name, COUNT(DISTINCT e.employee_id) AS employee_count, COUNT(be.enrollment_id) AS completed_q1_enrollments FROM departments d INNER JOIN employees e ON d.department_id = e.department_id LEFT JOIN benefit_enrollments be ON e.employee_id = be.employee_id AND be.enrollment_status = 'completed' AND be.submitted_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' AND be.submitted_date < DATE '2024-04-01' WHERE e.hire_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' GROUP BY d.department_id, d.department_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT e.employee_id) > 0 ORDER BY d.department_name;

_meta.scenario: an HR platform tracking onboarding completion and benefits enrollment
